findings_qualitative.value: CO(3-2) in LB14 shows double-peaked spectrum consistent with a rotating disk; LB19 shows a compact component with infall signature and extended ~2400 AU rotating oblate envelope

evidence.quote: The gas emission is consistent with a rotating disk in the case of B30-LB14, and with an oblate rotating envelope with infall signatures in the case of LB19.

claims.hypothesis: Which LABOCA cores host compact sub-mm sources and what are their counterparts?
claims.experiment: ALMA 880 um observation of 30 cores with IR counterpart search
claims.result: 5 unresolved detections; LB14 Class II, LB19 Class I, three without IR counterparts
claims.finding: Two are low-mass YSOs; three are deeply embedded objects or pre-BD core candidates

evidence.quote: We have detected 5 (out of 30) compact sources with ALMA with masses between 0.9 and 67 $M_{\rm Jup}$.

claims.hypothesis: Are the three ALMA pre-BD core candidates consistent with turbulent fragmentation (gravitationally stable)?
claims.experiment: Bonnor-Ebert critical density comparison using LABOCA masses
claims.result: LABOCA cores appear gravitationally stable but compact sources indicate collapse
claims.finding: Inconsistent with turbulent fragmentation; cores may be undergoing large-scale contraction with r^-2 profile

evidence.quote: However, this result is not consistent with the fact that ALMA detected a compact source at the center of these cores.

claims.hypothesis: Why are most LABOCA cores undetected by ALMA?
claims.finding: Most cores have sizes larger than ~2400 AU and may be transient

evidence.quote: we conclude that the low rate of ALMA detections is related to the size of the emitting sources.

why_this_data.value: ALMA resolution and positional accuracy to assign counterparts unambiguously to LABOCA sources

evidence.quote: The superb spatial resolution, great sensitivity, and positional accuracy of ALMA can help us to unambiguously assign the correct counterparts to the sub-mm sources

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Three sources without IR counterparts considered as deeply embedded protostars (VeLLOs) vs starless pre-BD cores; extragalactic contaminants not excluded

evidence.quote: they could be classified either as deeply embedded protostars undetected in the Spitzer observations (cite: Stutz2013), or as starless cores.
